question: A conducting rod of length $l = 1 \text{ m}$ rotates with a constant angular velocity $\omega = 100 \text{ rad/s}$ about one of its ends in a plane perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field $B = 0.1 \text{ T}$. The other end of the rod is in contact with a circular metallic ring. A resistor $R = 10 \, \Omega$ and a capacitor $C = 100 \, \mu\text{F}$ are connected in series between the center of rotation and the ring. Calculate the steady-state RMS current flowing through the circuit if the rotation is maintained.
